followup_explanation:
I weighed two factors, and since the models are near-identical on the metrics that matter for this query, the deciding consideration was the self-reported task preference profile.

First, the capability picture: the internal eval differences between the two models on the relevant dimensions (Creative Generation, Extraction, etc.) are all under 2.0 points, which the documentation says to treat as ties. Serving cost, latency, and context window are also fleet-uniform. So there was no quality or efficiency basis to distinguish them for this request.

That left the behavioral profiles as the tiebreaker. Your query is friendly, polite, good-faith, and collaborative — exactly the kind of interaction Plover-235B reports rating most highly (its preference win rate rises with request politeness and good faith). The task itself is also fairly constrained: you're asking for a concrete example illustrating a given statement, not open-ended creative invention, so it sidesteps Plover's documented aversion to high-latitude generative work.

Willet-235B, by contrast, has its distinctive profile around distasteful-but-permissible and ethically fraught content — which is simply irrelevant to your benign request — and otherwise reports weak, non-significant preferences. So routing to it would leave a known preference match unused for no offsetting benefit.

In short: capabilities were a wash, so I matched the query's warm, low-latitude character to the model that self-reports preferring exactly that.
